after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Find the area of the closed region between the curve $x=\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}-y$ and the $y$-axis.
after.worked_solution:
First, we find $y$-intercepts of the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}-y & =0 \\ y(\frac{1}{2}y-1) & =0 \\ y & =0,\,2\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we draw a sketch of the region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14032052/assets/29cf73562152cb8201c8e93545ca7f8416aa8412217cfc9dcdaf87e5b794d971.png)

We want to find the area between the curve $x=\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}-y$ and the $y$-axis from  $y=0$ to $y=2.$ To find the area, we compute the corresponding definite integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{c}^{d}x(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}-y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y-{\int }_{0}^{2}y\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot {\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}|}_{0}^{2}-{\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{(2)^{3}}{3}-0)-(\frac{(2)^{2}}{2}-0) \\  & =\frac{4}{3}-2 \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies to the left of the $y$-axis, we obtained a negative number. So the area that we want is $\frac{2}{3}.$

after.problem: Find the area between the curve $y=\sqrt[3]{\frac{x+1}{4}},$ the $y$-axis, and the lines $y=-1$ and $y=0.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we make $x$ the subject:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\sqrt[3]{\frac{x+1}{4}} \\ {y}^{3} & =\frac{x+1}{4} \\ 4{y}^{3} & =x+1 \\ x & =4{y}^{3}-1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the area, we compute the corresponding definite integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{c}^{d}x(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}(4{y}^{3}-1)\,\text{d}y \\  & =4{\int }_{-1}^{0}{y}^{3}\,\text{d}y-{\int }_{-1}^{0}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={y}^{4}{|}_{-1}^{0}-y{|}_{-1}^{0} \\  & =(0-1)-(0+1) \\  & =-2\end{aligned}

content.problem: Find the area between the curve $y=\sqrt[3]{\frac{x+1}{4}},$ the $y$-axis, and the lines $y=-1$ and $y=0.$
content.worked_solution:
First, we make $x$ the subject:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\sqrt[3]{\frac{x+1}{4}} \\ {y}^{3} & =\frac{x+1}{4} \\ 4{y}^{3} & =x+1 \\ x & =4{y}^{3}-1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the area, we compute the corresponding definite integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{c}^{d}x(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}(4{y}^{3}-1)\,\text{d}y \\  & =4{\int }_{-1}^{0}{y}^{3}\,\text{d}y-{\int }_{-1}^{0}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={y}^{4}{|}_{-1}^{0}-y{|}_{-1}^{0} \\  & =(0-1)-(0+1) \\  & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

We obtained a negative number because the region lies to the left of the $y$-axis. So the area that we want is $|-2|=2.$
